/t, d/ deletion

Source: R/data.R
td_deletion.Rd

Whether word-final /t, d/ is deleted (as in wes' side), 50 tokens from each of 40 speakers. Includes an interaction, a non-linear age effect, correlated predictors and two pure-noise predictors. For classification trees and random forests.

Usage

td_deletion

Format

A tibble with 2000 rows and 11 columns:

speaker

S01 to S40.

deleted

"retained" or "deleted".

following

Following segment: "vowel", "pause" or "consonant".

morph

"monomorpheme" (mist) or "past" (missed).

rate

Speech rate in syllables per second.

log_freq

log10 word frequency, 1 to 6.

age

Speaker age, 18 to 80.

gender

"female" or "male"; no effect.

education

"school" or "university"; correlated with age but no effect of its own.

noise_cont, noise_bin

Random noise, continuous and binary; no effect.

Source

data-raw/td_deletion.R

Details

True model, in log-odds of deletion: -0.8 + s0 + 1.8 * consonant + 0.4 * pause - 1 * past + 0.9 * (rate - 5) * consonant + 1.2 * plogis((45 - age) / 5) + 0.25 * (log_freq - 3.5), with by-speaker intercepts s0 of SD 0.5. Rate matters only before consonants; deletion drops sharply around age 45.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("rpart", quietly = TRUE)) {
  tree <- rpart::rpart(deleted ~ following + morph + rate + log_freq + age + gender +
                         education + noise_cont + noise_bin, data = td_deletion)
  round(tree$variable.importance)
}
#>  following        age       rate   log_freq  education      morph noise_cont 
#>         85         39         27         22         19          6          2 
#>  noise_bin 
#>          1 
if (requireNamespace("randomForest", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  rf <- randomForest::randomForest(deleted ~ following + morph + rate + log_freq + age +
                                     gender + education + noise_cont + noise_bin,
                                   data = td_deletion, importance = TRUE)
  round(randomForest::importance(rf, type = 1), 1)
}
#>            MeanDecreaseAccuracy
#> following                  62.4
#> morph                      22.6
#> rate                       10.4
#> log_freq                   10.1
#> age                        28.9
#> gender                      5.0
#> education                  12.3
#> noise_cont                  2.2
#> noise_bin                  -0.2
